recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.
formula_note: Another a sinx + b cosx = c equation. Dividing by √(a² + b²) here regroups the ratios into a single cosine term, cos(x − π/6) = cos(π/4), so the finishing formula is the cosine form x = 2nπ ± α. Whether an equation like this ends in the cosine form or the sine form nπ + (−1)ⁿα depends on how the ratios pair up, not on how the question looks.

steps.label: Divide by √(a² + b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark. Here a = 1 and b = √3, so √(1 + 3) = 2. Dividing by 2 makes the squares of the coefficients add to 1 (1/4 + 3/4 = 1), so they are the sine and cosine of one angle.
steps.memory_tip: a = 1 and b = √3, so √(1 + 3) = 2. Divide BOTH sides by 2, not by 4.

recall.must_convey: That both sides are divided by √(1 + 3) = 2.

steps.why: Without dividing, the coefficients 1 and √3 are not a sine and cosine of anything. Dividing by 2 makes them ½ and √3/2, which are.

steps.label: Combine into one cosine
steps.margin_note: Second mark. ½ = sin 30° and √3/2 = cos 30°, so the left side is cos x cos(π/6) + sin x sin(π/6) = cos(x − π/6).
steps.memory_tip: ½ = sin 30° and √3/2 = cos 30°, so the left side is cos x cos(π/6) + sin x sin(π/6) = cos(x − π/6).

recall.must_convey: That the left side is recognised as cos(x − π/6), and the right side as 1/√2.

steps.why: cos X cos Y + sin X sin Y = cos(X − Y) — matching that pattern is the point of the division. One ratio can be solved; a sum of two cannot.
common_mistakes: Matching the sine pattern and getting sin(x + π/6).

steps.label: Find the principal value
steps.margin_note: Third mark. 1/√2 = cos(π/4), so the principal value is α = π/4.
steps.memory_tip: √2/2 is 1/√2, which is cos(π/4). So the principal value is π/4.

recall.must_convey: That 1/√2 = cos(π/4), so the principal value is π/4.
accept: one over root two is cos pi by four so the principal value is pi by four

steps.why: A general solution needs a named principal value to build on. Leaving the right side as 1/√2 gives nothing to write the general solution around.
common_mistakes: Writing the principal value as π/3.

steps.label: Write the general solution
steps.margin_note: Last mark. For a cosine equation the general solution is θ = 2nπ ± α, so x − π/6 = 2nπ ± π/4.
steps.memory_tip: Cosine equation, so 2nπ ± α. Then add the π/6 back to reach x.

steps.why: The cosine form uses 2nπ ± α; the sine form uses nπ + (−1)ⁿα. Using the wrong one here gives a set that contains angles which do not solve the equation and misses some that do.
